shared_elements: quadruped/animal shown in profile in low relief
horizontal band or line running across the pillar face
carved hand or fingers at the pillar edge (A: hands/arms area; B: fingers at right edge)
relief figures set on the broad face of an upright slab-like pillar
justification: Both surfaces carve schematic profile animals in shallow flat relief on the face of an upright slab, each combined with a long horizontal band crossing the pillar below the animals and with an angular zigzag element, and both include carved hands/fingers at the stone's edge, which is a fairly specific combination. The biggest difference in content is density and repertoire: A is a crowded multi-register composition with a row of arched animal figures, birds, a snake and net-like patterning, while B shows a single isolated quadruped above an almost empty field with one sweeping band.
